title: Iterated Ex gives a Kan replacement preserving finite limits
statement:
Use simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $\operatorname{Sd}(\Delta^n)$ be the ordinary nerve of the poset of nonempty subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ ordered by inclusion. Define $(\operatorname{Ex}K)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{Sd}(\Delta^n),K)$ with operators induced by image of subsets under monotone maps. The map sending a subset to its largest element gives a natural last-vertex map $\operatorname{Sd}(\Delta^n)\to\Delta^n$, and hence $j_K:K\to\operatorname{Ex}K$. Define
$$\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}K=\operatorname{colim}\bigl(K\xrightarrow{j_K}\operatorname{Ex}K\xrightarrow{j_{\operatorname{Ex}K}}\operatorname{Ex}^2K\longrightarrow\cdots\bigr).$$
Then $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}K$ is Kan for every $K$, the natural map $K\to\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}K$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, and the functor $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}$ preserves finite limits. Preservation of finite products means that the canonical maps to the products of the images, including the terminal-object comparison, are isomorphisms; these canonical comparisons and the natural unit commute with product projections.
